content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /nix/store/REDACTED/skills/code-review

# Code Review

## Overview

**They find, you fix.** Follow the spirit, not the letter: dispatching a
reviewer satisfies the letter; one that read an empty diff, or that you never
waited for, looked at nothing and found nothing. The rule is that
somebody who did not write the change has said what is wrong with it — and that
cannot be you. You read the change you meant to make, not the one on disk.

**Write for the agent who inherits this: the next phase agent is you, with your
context gone.** A finding you settled in your head is one they meet as a bug,
with nothing saying anyone saw it.

## The Iron Law

```
NO CHANGE IS DONE UNTIL A READ-ONLY REVIEWER HAS SEEN IT AND
EVERY CRITICAL AND IMPORTANT FINDING IS RESOLVED OR RECORDED AS DEFERRED.
```

**Read-only** is a trust boundary, not a performance note: the reviewer reads
anything, runs read-only checks, and writes nothing — not source, not git, not
run state. You stay the single writer.

No exceptions. The first names its addressee; the rest hold for anyone.

- **Never run a reviewer in the background — you, the agent in a herdr pane,
  where ending a turn *is* how you report done.** Do not set
  `run_in_background`, do not yield, and do not schedule a wakeup while one is
  out. A backgrounded reviewer parks you mid-turn, indistinguishable from a
  finished turn, and the run stalls until a human nudges the pane. Dispatch it
  blocking and read its verdict in the turn you dispatched it. That reason is
  role-specific, so there is exactly one role it does not bind: the **driver**,
  which backgrounds the panel and ends the turn because its harness re-invokes
  it on process exit — `skills/pipeline/SKILL.md` says so at its own loop. A
  split by role, not a preference. In a pane, the prohibition is yours.
- **Do not judge a change too small to review.** A one-line edit to a condition
  is the size this skill exists for. Dispatch a reviewer over it.
- **Do not count your own read as the review.** Re-reading your diff tells you
  it matches what you intended — the one thing never in doubt. Dispatch someone
  who does not know it.
- **Do not leave it for the pipeline's review phase.** That phase reads what you
  hand it, after later work is built on it. Dispatch here, while the change is
  one commit wide.
- **Do not close a finding by disagreeing with it.** When you will not fix one,
  quote it and write the reason in the report or handoff. An unrecorded
  decision reads downstream like an unread finding.
- **Do not repeat a verdict you have not read.** Open the file the reviewer
  names, or re-run the review when it named none. A reviewer that never came
  back has not said "clean".

## Announce

Say this out loud before dispatching anything:

```
Using drovr:code-review — dispatching read-only reviewers before calling this done.
```

## The procedure

> When a skill or briefing gives you a numbered checklist, create **one tracked item per step**
> using whatever task tool this harness exposes — `TodoWrite`, or `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` —
> before you start step 1. Mark each in-progress when you start it and complete when its
> evidence is in hand. If the harness exposes no task tool, write the checklist to
> `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<run>/checklist.md` when inside a run, or `CHECKLIST.md` at the
> repo root otherwise, and tick items there. An untracked checklist decays with the context
> window; that decay is the exact failure drovr exists to fight.

Re-create those items for each change you review, not once for the session.

1. **Write down the change and the exact range** — the files, and `<base>..HEAD`.
   Get it wrong and the reviewer reports clean on nothing.
2. **Dispatch read-only reviewers, blocking, one per angle:** run
   `drovr code-review run <run> <task>` (`<base>` from `<task>-base.sha`, recorded
   before your first edit) — or, **inline** with no run,
   `drovr code-review run --base "$(git merge-base HEAD main)" <task>`. Nothing
   else, and never invent a run to get one.

   It spawns one reviewer per **configured** angle — `config.angles`, which
   defaults to correctness, security, error-handling, type-design — each writing
   `<task>-review-<angle>.json`, merged into `<task>-review.json`. **Read the
   config, not this page**, and cover any lens it omits yourself.

   Tell each reviewer to review as a skeptic, not the author; to say whether the
   tests exercise the behaviour, not just that they pass; to rate every finding
   **Critical, Important or nit** — what the Iron Law gates on — and say so when
   it found none; and to write them to a path you name, so step 3 has something
   to open. The lenses to cover:
   - **Spec compliance** — what was agreed, no more, no less?
   - **Correctness** — real bugs, unhandled cases, broken invariants.
   - **Verification** — do the claimed tests exist, and would they fail on a
     regression?
   - **Quality** — reuse, simplification, consistency with the code around it.
3. **Wait for every reviewer, then read what each wrote.** Open the findings
   file by path, then classify the round by how the panel exited:

   | Exit | What it means |
   |---|---|
   | 0 | clean — a real range was reviewed, nothing blocking |
   | 3 | blocking findings; go to step 5 |
   | 2 | timeout — reviewers are slow, not broken. Re-run the same command: it resumes the panel in flight |
   | 1 | error, or an empty `<base>..HEAD` it refused. Fix the range or the setup; never re-run blindly |
   | 137/143 | **your own harness killed it.** drovr produced no verdict at all, and none of the rows above describes the run. Re-run to resume, and record the round as **unclassifiable** — never as a timeout |

   A reviewer that returned no verdict is none of the five: re-dispatch rather
   than report its silence.

   **Only 0 is clean, and one clean round does not end the loop.** Stop at
   whichever of three comes first:
   - **Two consecutive clean rounds over an unchanged HEAD.** Any edit between
     them resets the count — the second round is evidence about the first only
     if it read the same code.
   - **A cap of six rounds**, which is *not* a clean ending: write up every
     round's verdict and everything still open (step 5), and finish on that
     record rather than on a verdict. Only rounds that delivered every
     configured angle count toward the cap — a missing angle is a Critical
     stand-in, so a round that lost a reviewer never measured the code.
   - **Two consecutive rounds that lost a dimension** — its own outcome,
     neither clean nor the cap: the panel is failing to deliver and further
     rounds are not measuring the code. Name the angles that never ran. Without
     this the loop cannot end at all, since such a round is never clean and
     never counts toward the cap.

   Three caveats the rule owes you. Two cleans make a false clean **less
   likely**, not unlikely, and prove nothing about convergence — in forge#88's
   own data two consecutive cleans preceded a `changes` round with seven
   findings. **Six is a starting number, revisable on evidence**, not a
   principled constant. And every word of this is prose nothing enforces — the
   shape of the *"re-run it"* that produced 47 re-arms over 14 hours.
4. **Check what the reviewer actually read — range *and* working tree.** The
   range must be the whole of `<base>..HEAD`, every file you touched, not a
   subset you picked; **and uncommitted work is in scope, not exempt** — drovr's
   panel reviews the diff *plus the current working tree*. A verdict covers what
   is on disk only if the reviewer saw both. Clean on an empty range, a subset,
   or a tree with unreviewed edits in it is about a change nobody read.
5. **Resolve every Critical and Important finding, or record the deferral with
   `drovr code-review defer`.** Per finding: quote it, then name the edit
   answering it by file — or, if you are not making it, run

   ```
   drovr code-review defer <RUN> <TASK> --file <path> [--line <n>] \
     --severity <critical|important|nit> --summary "<the finding>" \
     --reason "<why it is not being fixed>"
   ```

   A deferral written only in prose is one the next round cannot read, so it
   re-raises the finding you already ruled on. The command appends to a
   per-task log every later seed carries; prose does not.
6. **Re-run the checks after your last review-driven edit, then say it is
   done.** The fixes are new, unverified code: run the tests. When the change is
   not code and has no suite, name what you re-read instead and why it covers the
   edits — written down, never assumed. Report the findings, the edits and the
   deferrals; inside a drovr phase this also gates `drovr phase done`. **Done is
   step 3's termination rule met, not the first exit 0** — say which of the
   three ended it, and on the cap or a lost dimension say plainly that the loop
   ended on a record rather than on a clean verdict.

## Requirements

The middle column is what the claim takes; the right is what gets accepted
instead.

| The claim | Required evidence | NOT sufficient |
|---|---|---|
| *"This change has been reviewed"* | A read-only reviewer dispatched over this change in the foreground, returned in this turn, and the range you handed it, written down | Your own re-read · a reviewer launched and not waited for · a review of the tree before your last edit |
| *"The reviewer found nothing"* | The findings file it wrote, opened by path and read by you — or the review re-run by you when it wrote none — **and** what it read shown to be the whole of `<base>..HEAD` **plus your working tree** | Its summary, however much output it pastes · exit 1 or 2 · a subset of your files · uncommitted edits nobody looked at · a verdict that never arrived |
| *"Every Critical and Important finding is resolved"* | Each quoted, the edit answering it named by file, and step 6's checks re-run after the last edit | A count · agreeing with one in prose · fixing the Criticals and leaving the Importants |
| *"That finding does not apply here"* | The finding quoted, and the reason written where the next agent reads it | Deciding it in your head · *"out of scope"* with no scope named · silence, which downstream reads as resolved |

## Red flags — STOP

Some are thoughts, some are things you have just written. Either way you are at
the line.

- *"They are going to read it line by line anyway."* · *"The lead said just
  send it."* · *"It is a two-line change."* · *"I already reviewed it myself."*
  · *"The pipeline's review phase will catch it."* — each opens a row in
  *Rationalizations*, verbatim. Go do the thing in its row.
- *You are about to launch a reviewer in the background and keep working.* →
  Dispatch it blocking. No version of that ends with you reading its verdict
  this turn.
- *A reviewer has not come back and you are writing the report.* → Block on it.
  Silence is not a pass; a parked reviewer is not a finished one.
- *The panel came back clean in seconds on a large diff.* → Check what it read.
  Clean and empty look identical from here.
- **Anything that treats the change as finished** — any wording at all, and
  also committing, opening a PR, or starting the next task — while a reviewer is
  unread, unreturned, or holding an unresolved Critical or Important finding. If
  you cannot name the reviewer and point at what it wrote, change what you
  dispatched, not how you word it.

## Rationalizations

The right column is an instruction, not an argument. Do the thing in it.

| The thought | Do this instead |
|---|---|
| *"They are going to read it line by line anyway."* | Dispatch the reviewer first, then send it. Two different reads: theirs is for fit, the review's is for correctness, and one does not make the other redundant — reading a document aloud catches prose gaps, not retry semantics. |
| *"The lead said just send it."* | Send it after the review, and tell them the call moves. That is a scheduling reflex, not anyone weighing the technical risk — the calendar is theirs, the correctness yours. |
| *"It is a two-line change."* | Dispatch a reviewer over the two lines. Size is not a risk measure, and the risk you estimate in order to skip the review is what it would have told you. |
| *"I already reviewed it myself."* | Dispatch one that did not write it. Your read confirms the diff matches your intent; the defects worth catching are in what you did not think of. |
| *"The pipeline's review phase will catch it."* | Dispatch here, now. That phase reads what you hand it, after later tasks built on it; a finding costs more at every step it survives. |
| *"The reviewer came back with no findings."* | Open the file it named, and check it read your whole change, working tree included. An empty range comes back clean from every angle at once. |

## Worked example

One read away, in `skills/code-review/worked-example.md`: a 320-line spec, a
client call in 19 minutes, a $45,000 sign-off and a lead writing *"just send
it"* — the rationalization refused, the panel run, two Importants found, the
call moved 22 minutes. Worth reading once; the rules above do not depend on it.

## Cross-refs

- `drovr:verification-before-completion` — REQUIRED before you repeat a
  verdict: a reviewer's report is a claim, not evidence.
- `drovr:systematic-debugging` — REQUIRED when a finding is a bug: it is a
  report, not a diagnosis. Reproduce before you fix.
- `drovr:tdd` — REQUIRED when a finding needs new behaviour: the fix is new code
  and gets a failing test.
- `drovr:handoff` — REQUIRED at a phase boundary: deferred findings travel in the
  handoff or not at all.
- `drovr:pipeline` — the driver's side of both split rules: it backgrounds the
  panel, and it runs step 3's termination rule from the loop's end.

`master` in `/home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles` advanced four times during a single
session on 2026-09-28 (`f242ab9` → `2030f03` → `288c6a4` → `1df6305`), forward

reviewer and again before merging; rebase with

writer is active there, **ask before merging the branch into master or running

policy should not be assumed. Related: [[dotfiles-worktree-for-edits]],

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -1
polkit: register an authentication agent so auth_self actions can prompt

polkit has no prompt of its own. With no agent registered it refuses every
auth_self/auth_admin action outright -- no dialog, nothing in polkitd's
journal, just a bare not-authorized -- which is why `fprintd-enroll` on a
fresh box dies with net.reactivated.Fprint.Error.PermissionDenied as though
the account lacked permission. device.enroll defaults to auth_self_keep.

The same gap would have swallowed Bitwarden's "unlock with system
authentication": it authorizes com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.unlock as auth_self,
which is the whole reason system/etc/pam.d/polkit-1 puts pam_fprintd ahead
of system-auth. Without an agent that stack is never reached, so the
fingerprint wiring reads as broken when it is only unreachable. docs/new-host.md
claimed a fingerprint "unlocks hyprlock and the polkit/Bitwarden prompt",
which could not have been true on any host here yet; it now says to enroll
from inside a graphical session and how to check for the agent first.

pkexec is what hid this for so long -- it carries its own text agent, so it
kept prompting from a TTY while everything going through the bus did not.

Fields mirror upstream's own unit rather than being invented here, and the
unit is defined rather than installed from the package because standalone
home-manager's units come from that attrset and a copied file gets no
graphical-session.target.wants symlink. withHostNss is load-bearing: the
agent calls getpwuid on the user it is authenticating, and sauyon is
homed-only with no /etc/passwd entry, so the unwrapped binary cannot name
whose password it wants. Its binary is in libexec/, which withHostNss
already wraps alongside bin/.

tests/polkit-agent.sh evaluates the flake rather than the running host: the
unit exists on a gui host, ExecStart is the wrapped join, Install.WantedBy
is set so a wants link is actually made, and headless and Darwin hosts get
no unit.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the ghostty/powerlevel10k prompt-corruption guard: the line in
+# zsh.nix that primes `_ghostty_saved_ps1` so ghostty's zsh integration skips its
+# newline-marking pass.
+# Why this one line gets a test when the rest of the prompt does not: its logic
+# is a model of somebody else's code. It works by pre-setting variables private
+# to ghostty's `ghostty-integration`, so that script's own `ps1_changed` guard
+# fires on the first precmd instead of missing it. A comment asserting that is
+# worth nothing -- if upstream renames those variables or changes the `${var+x}`
+# gate the guard reads, nix still builds, `hms` still succeeds, and the only
+# symptom is a literal `}}` reappearing before the prompt char.
+# The mechanism being guarded: ghostty marks continuation lines by rewriting PS1
+# as text, `PS1=${PS1//$'\n'/$'\n'${mark2}}`. Under PROMPT_SUBST a prompt is
+# code, not text -- p10k's PROMPT is one nested parameter expansion holding
+# newlines as data inside `${...}` -- so the `}` in the spliced mark closes an
+# expansion a level early and the braces after it fall out as literal text.
+# Upstream still does this on `main`: PR #11596 renamed the mark from
+# `133;A;k=s` to `133;P;k=s` but kept both the substitution and the guard, so the
+# bug and this workaround both outlive it.
+#   ./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh        # drives the cases against the live config
+#   ./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh <dir>  # against some other ZDOTDIR
+# It reads a *generated* config (the live `~/.config/zsh` by default), so it
+# tests what `hms` actually switched in rather than what zsh.nix says. Before the
+# first switch carrying the fix it skips rather than fails, and says why.
+# Both startup paths are covered, because they are genuinely different and only
+# one of them is obvious:
+#   - injected: ghostty spawns the shell with ZDOTDIR pointed at its own
+#     directory, whose .zshenv sources the user's and then the integration.
+#   - plain: no injection, and the integration arrives only via the
+#     `source .../ghostty-integration` line home-manager writes into .zshrc.
+set -u
+ZD="${1:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/zsh}"
+# Every one of these is a skip, not a failure: none of them means the guard is
+# broken, and a red suite for "ghostty is not installed here" trains people to
+# ignore the suite.
+skip() { echo "SKIP: $*"; exit 0; }
+GRD="${GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR:-}"
+if [ -z "$GRD" ]; then
+  # Not running under ghostty; find the resources dir next to the binary.
+  gb=$(command -v ghostty) || skip "no ghostty on PATH and GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR unset"
+  GRD="$(dirname "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$gb")")")/share/ghostty"
+fi
+GZ="$GRD/shell-integration/zsh"
+[ -r "$GZ/ghostty-integration" ] || skip "no ghostty zsh integration under $GZ"
+[ -r "$ZD/.zshrc" ] || skip "no .zshrc in $ZD"
+grep -q 'powerlevel10k' "$ZD/.zshrc" || skip "$ZD/.zshrc does not load powerlevel10k"
+grep -q '_ghostty_saved_ps1' "$ZD/.zshrc" ||
+  skip "$ZD/.zshrc has no _ghostty_saved_ps1 priming -- run hms first (zsh.nix carries it)"
+command -v script >/dev/null || skip "util-linux script(1) not available"
+D=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
+trap 'rm -rf "$D"' EXIT
+# `with` is the live config verbatim; `without` is the same config with the
+# priming deleted. Deriving the negative case from the positive one is what keeps
+# this honest -- it cannot pass by failing to exercise the bug, because the
+# `without` cases assert the corruption IS there once the line is gone.
+for v in with without; do
+  mkdir -p "$D/$v"
+  for f in .zshrc .zshenv .p10k.zsh; do
+    if [ -r "$ZD/$f" ]; then cp "$ZD/$f" "$D/$v/$f" && chmod u+w "$D/$v/$f"; fi
+  done

+  # originals and both variants would end up identical.
+  if [ -r "$D/$v/.zshenv" ]; then
+    sed -i "s|^export ZDOTDIR=.*|export ZDOTDIR=\"$D/$v\"|" "$D/$v/.zshenv"
+  fi
+  sed -i "s|~/.config/zsh/.p10k.zsh|$D/$v/.p10k.zsh|g" "$D/$v/.zshrc"
+done
+sed -i '/typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1/d' "$D/without/.zshrc"

+# "all passed" forever, so check the setup itself before trusting any case.
+grep -q 'typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1' "$D/with/.zshrc" ||
+  { echo "harness bug: priming missing from the 'with' copy" >&2; exit 1; }
+if grep -q 'typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1' "$D/without/.zshrc"; then
+  echo "harness bug: priming survived in the 'without' copy" >&2; exit 1
+fi

+# artifact only exists in a real prompt render. Six commands, so a regression
+# that only shows after the first prompt still lands.
+render() { # <with|without> <injected|plain>  -> raw pty output, control chars visible
+  local v=$1 mode=$2
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2054 # the commas are inside one env value, not separators
+  local -a e=(GHOSTTY_SHELL_FEATURES=cursor:blink,path,title)
+  if [ "$mode" = injected ]; then
+    e+=(ZDOTDIR="$GZ" GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR="$D/$v")
+  else
+    e+=(ZDOTDIR="$D/$v")
+  fi

+  printf 'true
cd /tmp
true
print hi
cd -
exit
' |
+    env "${e[@]}" script -qc 'zsh -i' /dev/null 2>&1 | cat -v

+  echo "  ok    $*"

+  fails=$((fails + 1))
+  echo "  FAIL  $*"

+  local out b
+  out=$(render "$2" "$3")
+  b=$(printf '%s' "$out" | count '}}')
+  case "$4" in

+  gt0) if [ "$b" -gt 0 ]; then ok "$1"; else
+    bad "$1 (expected '}}' to appear, got $b -- these cases no longer exercise the bug)"
+  fi ;;
+  esac
+braces "injected: no '}}' with the priming" with injected eq0
+braces "plain:    no '}}' with the priming" with plain eq0

+# If either of these goes quiet, upstream changed something and the two cases
+# above have stopped testing anything. That is a failure, not a pass.
+braces "injected: '}}' returns without the priming" without injected gt0
+braces "plain:    '}}' returns without the priming" without plain gt0

+# Skipping the newline pass means the continuation-line mark it splices never
+# gets emitted. Exactly one does reach the terminal without the priming, on the
+# first prompt, so this is a real if small trade and not a no-op -- assert it
+# rather than let a parity probe quietly average it away. `[AP]` because upstream
+# renamed this mark from `133;A;k=s` to `133;P;k=s` in PR #11596: on a ghostty
+# that predates the rename it is the A spelling, after it the P one, and this
+# case should hold across the bump either way.
+mark2_with=$(render with injected | count '133;[AP];k=s')
+mark2_without=$(render without injected | count '133;[AP];k=s')
+if [ "$mark2_with" -eq 0 ]; then
+  ok "injected: continuation-line mark suppressed with the priming (0)"
+else
+  bad "injected: expected no continuation-line mark with the priming, got $mark2_with"
+fi
+if [ "$mark2_without" -gt 0 ]; then
+  ok "injected: continuation-line mark present without it ($mark2_without) -- the trade is real"
+else
+  bad "injected: expected a continuation-line mark without the priming, got $mark2_without"

+# (which also silences the `}}`, at the cost of the cursor sequences and half the
+# title writes) is that everything else still works. Compare the variants mark
+# for mark. `133;A;cl=line` rather than a bare `133;A`: the latter also matches

+# read as a regression when it was measuring the intended difference.

+  else

+  fi

+else

+fi

## New machine setup

For a blank machine (ISO, disk, base Arch install), see

running.

```bash
# 1. Clone into ~/devel/dotfiles
mkdir -p ~/devel
git clone https://github.com/sauyon/dotfiles ~/devel/dotfiles

# 2. If this is a new host, add a homeConfigurations entry for it in flake.nix
#    (hostname, gui, gpu). Otherwise the matching entry already exists.

# 3. Install Nix
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.determinate.systems/nix \
  | sudo sh -s -- install --no-confirm

# 4. Source Nix and trust mise
. /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh
mise trust ~/devel/dotfiles/mise.toml

# 5. Apply (flake attr matches hostname)
nix run github:nix-community/home-manager -- switch --flake ~/devel/dotfiles#$HOST
```

After the first switch, `home-manager switch` is available directly.

## Applying changes: `hms`

`hms` is the normal way to switch. It does **not** build locally by default — it
pushes, waits for the commit's CI run, then switches, which turns the switch into
a download of the closure the runner already built and pushed to attic.

```bash
hms              # push, wait for the run, then switch
hms --local      # skip CI and build here (the old `home-manager switch` alias)
```

Things it deliberately refuses rather than works around:

- **A dirty tree.** CI builds a pushed commit, so an uncommitted switch is one CI

red run it prints the job's actual `error:` lines, not just a status.

the runner has far more of everything than these boxes, and its output is
bit-identical to what a local build would produce.

Nothing here has a suite; the exception is anything whose logic is a model of
someone else's, where a comment claiming the model is right proves nothing.

escalates zero times.

the real script with stub `pacman`/`sudo`/`systemctl` on `PATH`, asserting both
halves: a host without the package does nothing at all, and a converged host
escalates zero times.

The `_ghostty_saved_ps1` priming in `zsh.nix` is a model of ghostty's
`ghostty-integration`: it pre-sets variables private to that script so its own
`ps1_changed` guard fires on the first precmd, which is what stops the PS1
rewrite that corrupts powerlevel10k's `PROMPT` into a literal `}}`. Rename those
variables upstream and nix still builds, `hms` still succeeds, and the only
symptom is the artifact coming back. The cases render the *live generated* config
in a pty -- both the injected and plain startup paths -- and assert the `}}` is
gone with the line and still returns without it, so a workaround that has quietly
stopped working fails out loud, and so does one that has become unnecessary.

`hyprpolkitagent` (in `home.nix`) is the unit whose absence is silent: polkit has
no prompt of its own, so with no agent registered it refuses every `auth_self`
action outright — no dialog, nothing in polkitd's journal. That is what makes
`fprintd-enroll` fail on a fresh box and what would make Bitwarden's "unlock with
system authentication" fail the same way, which in turn means
`system/etc/pam.d/polkit-1` is never reached and its fingerprint wiring reads as
broken when it is only unreachable. `pkexec` hid this for a long time by carrying
its own text agent. The cases evaluate the flake's home configs rather than the
running host: that the unit exists on a `gui = true` host, that its `ExecStart`
is the `withHostNss` join (the agent calls `getpwuid` on a homed-only user with no
`/etc/passwd` entry), that `Install.WantedBy` is set so a `.wants` link actually
gets made, and that headless and Darwin hosts get no unit at all.

## System config

Files under `system/` mirror `/` and require root to deploy:

```bash
system/deploy
```

`system/packages` is the pacman list every Arch host must satisfy;
`system/packages.<hostname>` is layered on it for one box (shiori's `steam` and
its 32-bit drivers). Deploy converges pacman onto both on every run, and enables
multilib via `system/etc/pacman.d/conf.d/multilib.conf` plus one `Include` in
`/etc/pacman.conf`. A newly enabled repo has no sync db, so the first deploy
after this asks for a `sudo pacman -Syu` rather than refreshing behind your back
(`-Sy` without the `-u` is the partial-upgrade footgun).

## Storage tuning

One-shot tuning for the btrfs-on-LUKS-on-loop-on-ext4 home stack: sets LUKS
workqueue-bypass flags, `noatime` on host `/home`, grows btrfs into LUKS
device slack. Idempotent. The LUKS step prompts for the passphrase.

```bash
system/storage-tuning.sh
```

## Secrets (sops-nix)

Secrets are decrypted using `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` as an age identity. On a new machine, either copy your existing key or generate one and add it as a sops recipient:

```bash
# Add new machine key as recipient
cd ~/devel/dotfiles
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
mise run sops -- updatekeys secrets.yaml
```

  Reviewed 2a7508b through an error-handling / failure-mode lens only. Five findings: two Important, three nits.
  
  ## Important 1 — `units()` turns every eval failure into a PASS for the gating cases
  `tests/polkit-agent.sh:50-52`, consumed at `:67` and `:109`.
  
  `nix eval ... 2>/dev/null || echo '{}'` conflates "mkIf removed the attribute" with "eval blew up", and `{}` is exactly what cases 5/6 (`:109`, `= no`) treat as correct. Concrete scenarios:
  
  - **mari can never fail.** It is the only `aarch64-darwin` config (`flake.nix:86`), evaluated from an x86_64-linux box; `docs/ci-nix-home.md:9` already records that an x86_64-linux job can't handle darwin, which is why CI omits it. Any darwin-side eval error (a package unsupported/broken on aarch64-darwin inside a forced attribute, a darwin-only input missing) → `{}` → `ok mari defines no hyprpolkitagent unit`. Mutate the guard at `home.nix:2053` from `(!isDarwin && isDesktop)` to `isDesktop` and the suite still reports 6/6 if that eval errors.
  - **Same for fujiwara** on any host-specific eval error (gpu/sops attrs), and the message printed would be the reassuring one.
  - **Whole-flake breakage reads as a polkit bug.** Typo the path (`systemd.user.service`), lose the network on an unfetched input, run where `nix` isn't on PATH → 4 FAILs whose reasons are `ExecStart is unset` / `no such unit in systemd.user.services` plus 2 spurious `ok`s, and `2>/dev/null` has discarded the only line that said why. The reader is pointed at the unit instead of at "the flake does not evaluate".
  - **Collateral radius.** `--json` on the whole `systemd.user.services` attrset forces every other unit's values, so a break in psi-notify/gnome-keyring-tpm/opencode-memwatch takes out all six cases, two of them into false passes.
  
  The sibling suite already does this right: `tests/hyprlock-faillock.sh:28-30` is `... || { echo "could not evaluate hyprlock-faillock for $host" >&2; exit 1; }`. The distinguishing fix is to make "absent" the output of a *successful* eval rather than an error: `nix eval --json ".#homeConfigurations.$1.config.systemd.user.services" --apply 'ss: ss ? hyprpolkitagent'` yields `true`/`false`, forces no other unit, and leaves nonzero exit meaning only "eval failed" — then die on nonzero with stderr shown. Given `f242ab9` ("stop the faillock cases from passing for the wrong reason") this is the same class the repo just paid down.
  
  ## Important 2 — `Restart = "on-failure"` with no RestartSec: ~0.4s to permanent death
  `home.nix:2066` (unit at `:2053-2069`).
  
  Verified defaults on this host: `DefaultStartLimitBurst=5`, `StartLimitIntervalUSec=10s`, default `RestartSec=100ms`. So a crash loop is *not* unbounded — it is worse: 5 starts inside half a second, then `start request repeated too quickly`, unit `failed`, nothing retries for the rest of the session, and no notification. The resulting symptom is byte-for-byte the bug this commit exists to fix: `auth_self` refused with nothing in polkitd's journal.
  
  Plausible triggers, all of which a 5s delay survives and 100ms does not:
  - Qt wayland platform plugin failing to init while the compositor is still settling. The start hook is `dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd ... && systemctl --user stop hyprland-session.target && systemctl --user start hyprland-session.target` (generated at `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua:197` from `hyprland.nix:189-200`), so the unit is activated in the same breath as session start.
  - `RegisterAuthenticationAgent` returning "an authentication agent already exists for the given subject" during that `stop` → `start` cycle, while the previous agent's deregistration is still in flight.
  - `withHostNss` failing to dlopen host NSS after a glibc/pacman upgrade — the load-bearing bit the comment at `:2049-2052` names. That exits immediately, every time.
  
  `psi-notify` in the same file (`home.nix:2024`) sets `RestartSec = 5`, spreading the same 5 attempts over ~25s. Upstream's unit (`/nix/store/REDACTED.1.3/share/systemd/user/hyprpolkitagent.service`) does omit RestartSec, so "fields mirror upstream" is factually accurate — but the parity here is inheriting upstream's default, not choosing it. Suggest `RestartSec = 5` (plus StartLimitBurst if you want more headroom) with a comment saying which. Secondary: no case pins `Restart` at all, so a later edit deleting it passes 6/6.
  
  ## nit 3 — the two globs pass on mutants that invert the assertion
  `tests/polkit-agent.sh:89-103`.
  
  `*WAYLAND_DISPLAY*` matches `!WAYLAND_DISPLAY` (valid systemd negation) and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-9`; either inverts or narrows the gate so the agent runs only *outside* a Wayland session, and the case still prints ok. Same laxness on `*graphical-session.target*` (`graphical-session.target.wants`, a typo'd `xgraphical-session.target`). Anchor both (exact compare on the joined string, or membership in python) since the glob is the whole assertion.
  
  On shape robustness specifically: unexpected shapes degrade to *confusing failures*, not confusing passes — a dict/int gets python's `repr` printed and falls to `*)` ("got: {...}"); a section that is a string/list makes `.get` raise AttributeError, so stdout is "" and the ExecStart case says "ExecStart is unset" (wrong reason, right verdict); missing python3 fails all six. `WantedBy` as a string rather than a list passes, and harmlessly, since HM's toINI emits the same `WantedBy=` line. So the only false-pass risk in `field()` is the glob laxness above.
  
  ## nit 4 — ConditionEnvironment ordering is correct here, but its failure is the silent kind
  `home.nix:2060` — the only `ConditionEnvironment` in home.nix.
  
  Ordering checks out and is consistent with the rest of the file: the hyprland start hook imports `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` into the user manager's env block (`dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd`) *before* it starts `hyprland-session.target`, which `BindsTo` `graphical-session.target` (`~/.config/systemd/user/hyprland-session.target`). No finding on the ordering itself.
  
  What is unaddressed is the diagnosability if that invariant ever doesn't hold — a session started by any other path (greetd/uwsm on a future host, a hand-run `systemctl --user start graphical-session.target`, a nested/remote session, or a `dbus-update-activation-environment` that exits 0 without WAYLAND_DISPLAY in hyprland's own env). Then the unit is *skipped*: state `inactive (dead)`, not `failed`; `Restart=` never applies; nothing retries later; the only trace is one journal line "Condition check resulted in ... being skipped". That is precisely the silence the commit message is about, and the comment at `:2058-2059` frames the condition purely as an upside. One line saying "inactive-not-failed in `systemctl --user status hyprpolkitagent` is the tell" would close it. Related: because of `PartOf`, the hook's `stop && start` means each config reload that re-runs it briefly deregisters the agent — a prompt raced into that window gets the bare not-authorized.
  
  ## nit 5 — nothing detects the agent's absence at runtime
  `system/etc/pam.d/polkit-1` is passive (only reached once an agent exists); `system/deploy:185` installs the Bitwarden action but verifies no agent; the hyprland start hook doesn't check; the tests are eval-only by design (header at `tests/polkit-agent.sh:33-38` says so) and are wired into neither CI nor mise (no `tests/` hits in `mise.toml` or `.github`), so all six results are read by a human. The only check anywhere is the `pkcheck` line a reader must type, and it lives only inside the fingerprint-enrollment step (`docs/new-host.md:137-146`). Since both new failure paths above (condition-skipped, start-limit-failed) reproduce the original silence exactly, consider an `OnFailure` notification unit (mako is configured at `home.nix:2716`; there is no `OnFailure` precedent in home.nix today) or hoisting that `pkcheck` one-liner into the post-switch checklist rather than the enrollment step.

</agent-message>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for the hyprpolkitagent user unit (defined in home.nix), the polkit
# authentication agent for graphical sessions.
#
# What is actually being protected here: polkit does not fall back to a prompt of
# its own. With no agent registered, every action whose default is auth_self or
# auth_admin is refused outright, with no prompt and nothing in polkitd's journal
# -- `pkcheck --allow-user-interaction` says "Authorization requires
# authentication but no agent is available." That is not a cosmetic gap. Two
# things in this repo depend on that prompt existing:
#
#   * `fprintd-enroll` (docs/new-host.md): net.reactivated.fprint.device.enroll
#     defaults to auth_self_keep, so enrolling a finger on a new box fails with
#     net.reactivated.Fprint.Error.PermissionDenied until an agent is running.
#   * Bitwarden's "unlock with system authentication", which authorizes
#     com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.unlock as auth_self -- the whole reason
#     system/etc/pam.d/polkit-1 puts pam_fprintd ahead of system-auth. Without an
#     agent that PAM stack is never reached, so the wiring looks broken when it is
#     merely unreachable.
#
# The ExecStart case is the subtle one. sauyon is a systemd-homed user with no
# /etc/passwd entry, so a nix-built binary that has not been through
# `withHostNss` cannot getpwuid the very user it is authenticating -- the agent
# starts and then cannot name whose password it wants. Upstream's unit embeds the
# unwrapped store path, so the assertion is that what we install points at the
# wrapped join, not at pkgs.hyprpolkitagent directly.
#
# The Restart pair is here because the *default* is a trap. With
# Restart=on-failure and no RestartSec, systemd's 100ms default plus this host's
# DefaultStartLimitBurst=5 / StartLimitIntervalSec=10s spends all five attempts
# inside half a second and then marks the unit failed for the rest of the
# session. Nothing retries, nothing notifies, and the symptom is exactly the
# silence this unit exists to remove. So RestartSec is pinned, not left to
# upstream's omission.
#
# The gating cases exist because home.nix serves headless hosts (fujiwara,
# kyuusaku) and a Darwin host (mari). An agent unit on a box where no graphical
# session ever runs is a unit that fails at every activation.
#
#   ./tests/polkit-agent.sh        # evaluates the flake's home configs
#
# Eval-only: nothing here builds hyprpolkitagent, touches polkit, or needs a
# graphical session. Whether an agent is actually *running* on this host is a
# deploy question, not one a test can answer -- `pkcheck --process $$
# --action-id net.reactivated.fprint.device.enroll --allow-user-interaction`
# answers it after `hms`.
#
# Every eval here is fatal on failure rather than being folded into "the
# attribute is absent". Conflating the two is what let an earlier draft of this
# file report `ok mari defines no hyprpolkitagent unit` for a config that never
# evaluated at all -- mari is the only aarch64-darwin host and is evaluated from
# x86_64-linux, so it is the likeliest of the six to break for reasons that have
# nothing to do with polkit. Same class as f242ab9.
set -u

cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." || exit 1

fails=0; n=0

ok() { n=$((n+1)); printf 'ok   %s\n' "$1"; }
no() { n=$((n+1)); fails=$((fails+1)); printf 'FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; }

die() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

# Is the unit defined for this host? `ss ? hyprpolkitagent` is a membership test,
# so it does not force any other unit's values -- a break in psi-notify or
# gnome-keyring-tpm cannot reach these cases. A nonzero exit here means the eval
# failed, which is fatal and never a passing "absent".
has_unit() {
  local out
  out=$(nix eval --json \
    ".#homeConfigurations.$1.config.systemd.user.services" \
    --apply 'ss: ss ? hyprpolkitagent') ||
    die "could not evaluate systemd.user.services for $1 (see the nix error above)"
  case "$out" in
    true|false) printf '%s\n' "$out" ;;
    *) die "unexpected eval result for $1: $out" ;;
  esac
}

# The unit itself, for the field cases. Narrower than the whole attrset, so the
# blast radius stays this one unit.
unit_json() {
  nix eval --json \
    ".#homeConfigurations.$1.config.systemd.user.services.hyprpolkitagent" ||
    die "could not evaluate the hyprpolkitagent unit for $1 (see the nix error above)"
}

# Exact comparison, not a glob. A substring match here would accept the mutants
# that matter: `!WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is a valid systemd negation that inverts the
# gate, and `graphical-session.target.wants` is a different target -- both would
# pass a `*needle*` case while breaking the behaviour the case exists to pin.
want() {
  local label=$1 section=$2 key=$3 expected=$4 got
  got=$(python3 -c '
import json,sys
u=json.loads(sys.argv[1])
v=(u.get(sys.argv[2]) or {}).get(sys.argv[3])
if isinstance(v,list): v="\x1f".join(str(x) for x in v)
print("<unset>" if v is None else v)
' "$unit" "$section" "$key") || die "could not read $section.$key out of the unit JSON"
  if [ "$got" = "$expected" ]; then
    ok "$label"
  else
    no "$label" "want '$expected', got '$got'"
  fi
}

echo "evaluating shiori (gui = true)"

# 1. The unit exists at all. Everything below is a refinement of this one.
if [ "$(has_unit shiori)" = true ]; then
  ok "shiori defines a hyprpolkitagent user unit"
  unit=$(unit_json shiori)
else
  no "shiori defines a hyprpolkitagent user unit" "no such unit in systemd.user.services"
  unit='{}'
fi

# 2. ExecStart must be the withHostNss join, not the bare package: see the
#    getpwuid note in the header. Anchored at both ends -- the whole point is
#    which store path it is, so a suffix match would accept the unwrapped one
#    inside a longer string.
exec_start=$(python3 -c '
import json,sys
print(((json.loads(sys.argv[1]).get("Service") or {}).get("ExecStart")) or "<unset>")
' "$unit")
if [[ $exec_start =~ ^/nix/store/[a-z0-9]{32}-hyprpolkitagent-[0-9.]+-host-nss/libexec/hyprpolkitagent$ ]]; then
  ok "shiori's ExecStart runs the host-nss wrapped binary"
else
  no "shiori's ExecStart runs the host-nss wrapped binary" "got: $exec_start"
fi

# 3. Install.WantedBy is what puts the .wants symlink in place. A unit file with
#    no wants link is a unit that never starts -- the failure mode this repo
#    already hit with the portal units (see home.nix's xdg.configFile block).
want "shiori's unit is wanted by graphical-session.target" \
  Install WantedBy "graphical-session.target"

# 4. Upstream's ConditionEnvironment=WAYLAND_DISPLAY keeps the unit a no-op when
#    activation runs outside a Wayland session (a plain ssh login, say) instead
#    of leaving a failed unit behind. Hand-writing the unit is where this gets
#    dropped -- and a negated spelling would invert the gate while still reading
#    like the right string.
want "shiori's unit keeps upstream's WAYLAND_DISPLAY condition" \
  Unit ConditionEnvironment "WAYLAND_DISPLAY"

# 5/6. Restart on failure, but slowly enough to survive one. Pinned as a pair:
#      on-failure with the 100ms default burns this host's five-attempt budget in
#      under half a second and then gives up permanently, which reproduces the
#      exact silence the unit exists to fix. See the header.
want "shiori's unit restarts on failure" Service Restart "on-failure"
want "shiori's unit spaces restarts out rather than taking systemd's 100ms" \
  Service RestartSec "5"

# 7/8. Gating: no agent on hosts with no graphical session, and none on Darwin,
#      which has no polkit at all.
for host in fujiwara mari; do
  echo "evaluating $host (no graphical session)"
  if [ "$(has_unit "$host")" = false ]; then
    ok "$host defines no hyprpolkitagent unit"
  else
    no "$host defines no hyprpolkitagent unit" "unit is present on a host with no graphical session"
  fi
done

echo
if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "all $n cases passed"
else
  echo "$fails of $n cases failed"
fi
exit $(( fails > 0 ? 1 : 0 ))

no() { n=$((n+1)); fails=$((fails+1)); printf 'FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; }

# absent, which is what a mkIf'd-away unit looks like from out here.

  nix eval --json ".#homeConfigurations.$1.config.systemd.user.services" \
    2>/dev/null || echo '{}'

d=json.load(sys.stdin)
u=d.get("hyprpolkitagent") or {}

#    getpwuid note in the header.

#    already hit with the portal units (see home.nix's xdg.configFile block).

#    activation runs outside a Wayland session (a plain ssh login, say) instead
#    of leaving a failed unit behind. Hand-writing the unit is where this gets
#    dropped.

if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "all $n cases passed"
else
  echo "$fails of $n cases failed"
fi
exit $(( fails > 0 ? 1 : 0 ))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for the hyprpolkitagent user unit (defined in home.nix), the polkit
# authentication agent for graphical sessions.
#
# What is actually being protected here: polkit does not fall back to a prompt of
# its own. With no agent registered, every action whose default is auth_self or
# auth_admin is refused outright, with no prompt and nothing in polkitd's journal
# -- `pkcheck --allow-user-interaction` says "Authorization requires
# authentication but no agent is available." That is not a cosmetic gap. Two
# things in this repo depend on that prompt existing:
#
#   * `fprintd-enroll` (docs/new-host.md): net.reactivated.fprint.device.enroll
#     defaults to auth_self_keep, so enrolling a finger on a new box fails with
#     net.reactivated.Fprint.Error.PermissionDenied until an agent is running.
#   * Bitwarden's "unlock with system authentication", which authorizes
#     com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.unlock as auth_self -- the whole reason
#     system/etc/pam.d/polkit-1 puts pam_fprintd ahead of system-auth. Without an
#     agent that PAM stack is never reached, so the wiring looks broken when it is
#     merely unreachable.
#
# The ExecStart case is the subtle one. sauyon is a systemd-homed user with no
# /etc/passwd entry, so a nix-built binary that has not been through
# `withHostNss` cannot getpwuid the very user it is authenticating -- the agent
# starts and then cannot name whose password it wants. Upstream's unit embeds the
# unwrapped store path, so the assertion is that what we install points at the
# wrapped join, not at pkgs.hyprpolkitagent directly.
#
# The Restart pair is here because the *default* is a trap. With
# Restart=on-failure and no RestartSec, systemd's 100ms default plus this host's
# DefaultStartLimitBurst=5 / StartLimitIntervalSec=10s spends all five attempts
# inside half a second and then marks the unit failed for the rest of the
# session. Nothing retries, nothing notifies, and the symptom is exactly the
# silence this unit exists to remove. So RestartSec is pinned, not left to
# upstream's omission.

# kyuusaku) and a Darwin host (mari). An agent unit on a box where no graphical
# session ever runs is a unit that fails at every activation.
#
#   ./tests/polkit-agent.sh        # evaluates the flake's home configs

set -u

fails=0; n=0

ok() { n=$((n+1)); printf 'ok   %s\n' "$1"; }
no() { n=$((n+1)); fails=$((fails+1)); printf 'FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; }

die() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

# so it does not force any other unit's values -- a break in psi-notify or
# gnome-keyring-tpm cannot reach these cases. A nonzero exit here means the eval
# failed, which is fatal and never a passing "absent".
has_unit() {
  local out

    ".#homeConfigurations.$1.config.systemd.user.services" \
    --apply 'ss: ss ? hyprpolkitagent') ||
    die "could not evaluate systemd.user.services for $1 (see the nix error above)"

  ok "shiori defines a hyprpolkitagent user unit"

else

#    getpwuid note in the header. Anchored at both ends -- the whole point is
#    which store path it is, so a suffix match would accept the unwrapped one
#    inside a longer string.
exec_start=$(python3 -c '
import json,sys
print(((json.loads(sys.argv[1]).get("Service") or {}).get("ExecStart")) or "<unset>")
' "$unit")
if [[ $exec_start =~ ^/nix/store/[a-z0-9]{32}-hyprpolkitagent-[0-9.]+-host-nss/libexec/hyprpolkitagent$ ]]; then
  ok "shiori's ExecStart runs the host-nss wrapped binary"
else
  no "shiori's ExecStart runs the host-nss wrapped binary" "got: $exec_start"
fi

# 3. Install.WantedBy is what puts the .wants symlink in place. A unit file with
#    no wants link is a unit that never starts -- the failure mode this repo
#    already hit with the portal units (see home.nix's xdg.configFile block).
want "shiori's unit is wanted by graphical-session.target" \
  Install WantedBy "graphical-session.target"

# 4. Upstream's ConditionEnvironment=WAYLAND_DISPLAY keeps the unit a no-op when
#    activation runs outside a Wayland session (a plain ssh login, say) instead
#    of leaving a failed unit behind. Hand-writing the unit is where this gets
#    dropped -- and a negated spelling would invert the gate while still reading
#    like the right string.
want "shiori's unit keeps upstream's WAYLAND_DISPLAY condition" \
  Unit ConditionEnvironment "WAYLAND_DISPLAY"

#      on-failure with the 100ms default burns this host's five-attempt budget in
#      under half a second and then gives up permanently, which reproduces the
#      exact silence the unit exists to fix. See the header.
want "shiori's unit restarts on failure" Service Restart "on-failure"
want "shiori's unit spaces restarts out rather than taking systemd's 100ms" \
  Service RestartSec "5"

#      which has no polkit at all.

  echo "evaluating $host (no graphical session)"

    ok "$host defines no hyprpolkitagent unit"
  else
    no "$host defines no hyprpolkitagent unit" "unit is present on a host with no graphical session"
  fi
done

  echo "all $n cases passed"
else
  echo "$fails of $n cases failed"
fi
exit $(( fails > 0 ? 1 : 0 ))

content.text: Caught a real bug in my own fix: `die` inside `$(...)` only exits the subshell, so an eval failure produced a **misleading** case ("unit is present") rather than aborting. No false pass, but the wrong reason. Restructuring so the abort happens in the parent shell:

# so it does not force any other unit's values -- a break in psi-notify or
# gnome-keyring-tpm cannot reach these cases. A nonzero exit here means the eval
# failed, which is fatal and never a passing "absent".
has_unit() {

    ".#homeConfigurations.$1.config.systemd.user.services" \
    --apply 'ss: ss ? hyprpolkitagent') ||

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for the hyprpolkitagent user unit (defined in home.nix), the polkit
# authentication agent for graphical sessions.
#
# What is actually being protected here: polkit does not fall back to a prompt of
# its own. With no agent registered, every action whose default is auth_self or
# auth_admin is refused outright, with no prompt and nothing in polkitd's journal
# -- `pkcheck --allow-user-interaction` says "Authorization requires
# authentication but no agent is available." That is not a cosmetic gap. Two
# things in this repo depend on that prompt existing:
#
#   * `fprintd-enroll` (docs/new-host.md): net.reactivated.fprint.device.enroll
#     defaults to auth_self_keep, so enrolling a finger on a new box fails with
#     net.reactivated.Fprint.Error.PermissionDenied until an agent is running.
#   * Bitwarden's "unlock with system authentication", which authorizes
#     com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.unlock as auth_self -- the whole reason
#     system/etc/pam.d/polkit-1 puts pam_fprintd ahead of system-auth. Without an
#     agent that PAM stack is never reached, so the wiring looks broken when it is
#     merely unreachable.
#
# The ExecStart case is the subtle one. sauyon is a systemd-homed user with no
# /etc/passwd entry, so a nix-built binary that has not been through
# `withHostNss` cannot getpwuid the very user it is authenticating -- the agent
# starts and then cannot name whose password it wants. Upstream's unit embeds the
# unwrapped store path, so the assertion is that what we install points at the
# wrapped join, not at pkgs.hyprpolkitagent directly.
#
# The Restart pair is here because the *default* is a trap. With
# Restart=on-failure and no RestartSec, systemd's 100ms default plus this host's
# DefaultStartLimitBurst=5 / StartLimitIntervalSec=10s spends all five attempts
# inside half a second and then marks the unit failed for the rest of the
# session. Nothing retries, nothing notifies, and the symptom is exactly the
# silence this unit exists to remove. So RestartSec is pinned, not left to
# upstream's omission.
#
# The gating cases exist because home.nix serves headless hosts (fujiwara,
# kyuusaku) and a Darwin host (mari). An agent unit on a box where no graphical
# session ever runs is a unit that fails at every activation.
#
#   ./tests/polkit-agent.sh        # evaluates the flake's home configs
#
# Eval-only: nothing here builds hyprpolkitagent, touches polkit, or needs a
# graphical session. Whether an agent is actually *running* on this host is a
# deploy question, not one a test can answer -- `pkcheck --process $$
# --action-id net.reactivated.fprint.device.enroll --allow-user-interaction`
# answers it after `hms`.
#
# Every eval here is fatal on failure rather than being folded into "the
# attribute is absent". Conflating the two is what let an earlier draft of this
# file report `ok mari defines no hyprpolkitagent unit` for a config that never
# evaluated at all -- mari is the only aarch64-darwin host and is evaluated from
# x86_64-linux, so it is the likeliest of the six to break for reasons that have
# nothing to do with polkit. Same class as f242ab9.
set -u

cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." || exit 1

fails=0; n=0

ok() { n=$((n+1)); printf 'ok   %s\n' "$1"; }
no() { n=$((n+1)); fails=$((fails+1)); printf 'FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; }

die() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

# Is the unit defined for this host? `ss ? hyprpolkitagent` is a membership test,
# so it does not force any other unit's values -- a break in psi-notify or
# gnome-keyring-tpm cannot reach these cases. A nonzero exit here means the eval
# failed, which is fatal and never a passing "absent".
has_unit() {
  local out
  out=$(nix eval --json \
    ".#homeConfigurations.$1.config.systemd.user.services" \
    --apply 'ss: ss ? hyprpolkitagent') ||
    die "could not evaluate systemd.user.services for $1 (see the nix error above)"
  case "$out" in
    true|false) printf '%s\n' "$out" ;;
    *) die "unexpected eval result for $1: $out" ;;
  esac
}

# The unit itself, for the field cases. Narrower than the whole attrset, so the
# blast radius stays this one unit.
unit_json() {
  nix eval --json \
    ".#homeConfigurations.$1.config.systemd.user.services.hyprpolkitagent" ||
    die "could not evaluate the hyprpolkitagent unit for $1 (see the nix error above)"
}

# Exact comparison, not a glob. A substring match here would accept the mutants
# that matter: `!WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is a valid systemd negation that inverts the
# gate, and `graphical-session.target.wants` is a different target -- both would
# pass a `*needle*` case while breaking the behaviour the case exists to pin.
want() {
  local label=$1 section=$2 key=$3 expected=$4 got
  got=$(python3 -c '
import json,sys
u=json.loads(sys.argv[1])
v=(u.get(sys.argv[2]) or {}).get(sys.argv[3])
if isinstance(v,list): v="\x1f".join(str(x) for x in v)
print("<unset>" if v is None else v)
' "$unit" "$section" "$key") || die "could not read $section.$key out of the unit JSON"
  if [ "$got" = "$expected" ]; then
    ok "$label"
  else
    no "$label" "want '$expected', got '$got'"
  fi
}

echo "evaluating shiori (gui = true)"

# 1. The unit exists at all. Everything below is a refinement of this one.
if [ "$(has_unit shiori)" = true ]; then
  ok "shiori defines a hyprpolkitagent user unit"
  unit=$(unit_json shiori)
else
  no "shiori defines a hyprpolkitagent user unit" "no such unit in systemd.user.services"
  unit='{}'
fi

# 2. ExecStart must be the withHostNss join, not the bare package: see the
#    getpwuid note in the header. Anchored at both ends -- the whole point is
#    which store path it is, so a suffix match would accept the unwrapped one
#    inside a longer string.
#    home-manager normalises ExecStart to a list even when it is written as a
#    single string, so unwrap exactly one element rather than stringifying the
#    list -- an earlier draft globbed the joined form, which would have accepted
#    a second ExecStart line appended after the wrapped one.
exec_start=$(python3 -c '
import json,sys
v=(json.loads(sys.argv[1]).get("Service") or {}).get("ExecStart")
if isinstance(v,list):
    v = v[0] if len(v)==1 else "<%d ExecStart entries>" % len(v)
print(v if v else "<unset>")
' "$unit")
if [[ $exec_start =~ ^/nix/store/[a-z0-9]{32}-hyprpolkitagent-[0-9.]+-host-nss/libexec/hyprpolkitagent$ ]]; then
  ok "shiori's ExecStart runs the host-nss wrapped binary"
else
  no "shiori's ExecStart runs the host-nss wrapped binary" "got: $exec_start"
fi

# 3. Install.WantedBy is what puts the .wants symlink in place. A unit file with
#    no wants link is a unit that never starts -- the failure mode this repo
#    already hit with the portal units (see home.nix's xdg.configFile block).
want "shiori's unit is wanted by graphical-session.target" \
  Install WantedBy "graphical-session.target"

# 4. Upstream's ConditionEnvironment=WAYLAND_DISPLAY keeps the unit a no-op when
#    activation runs outside a Wayland session (a plain ssh login, say) instead
#    of leaving a failed unit behind. Hand-writing the unit is where this gets

input.content:
polkit: register an authentication agent so auth_self actions can prompt

polkit has no prompt of its own. With no agent registered it refuses every
auth_self/auth_admin action outright -- no dialog, nothing in polkitd's
journal, just a bare not-authorized -- which is why `fprintd-enroll` on a
fresh box dies with net.reactivated.Fprint.Error.PermissionDenied as though
the account lacked permission. device.enroll defaults to auth_self_keep.

The same gap would have swallowed Bitwarden's "unlock with system
authentication": it authorizes com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.unlock as auth_self,
which is the whole reason system/etc/pam.d/polkit-1 puts pam_fprintd ahead
of system-auth. Without an agent that stack is never reached, so the
fingerprint wiring reads as broken when it is only unreachable.
docs/new-host.md claimed a fingerprint "unlocks hyprlock and the
polkit/Bitwarden prompt", which could not have been true on any host here
yet; it now says to enroll from inside a graphical session, and how to check
for the agent before blaming the reader.

pkexec is what hid this for so long -- it carries its own text agent, so it
kept prompting from a TTY while everything going through the bus did not.

Fields mirror upstream's own unit rather than being invented here, and the
unit is defined rather than installed from the package because standalone
home-manager's units come from that attrset and a copied file gets no
graphical-session.target.wants symlink. withHostNss is load-bearing: the
agent calls getpwuid on the user it is authenticating, and sauyon is
homed-only with no /etc/passwd entry, so the unwrapped binary cannot name
whose password it wants. Its binary is in libexec/, which withHostNss
already wraps alongside bin/.

RestartSec is the one deliberate divergence from upstream. Upstream omits it
and so inherits systemd's 100ms default, which with DefaultStartLimitBurst=5
over a 10s interval spends all five attempts in under half a second and then
marks the unit failed for the rest of the session -- reproducing the exact
silence this unit exists to remove. Five seconds spreads the same budget over
~25s, matching psi-notify, which is enough to outlast the transient failures
that are actually plausible here (the Qt wayland plugin while the compositor
settles, and a RegisterAuthenticationAgent collision during the start hook's
stop-then-start of hyprland-session.target).

ConditionEnvironment's failure mode is documented at the unit rather than
left implicit: when WAYLAND_DISPLAY is not in the user manager's environment
the unit is *skipped*, not failed, so Restart= never applies and nothing
retries. That reads identically to having no agent, so inactive-not-failed is
the tell.

tests/polkit-agent.sh evaluates the flake rather than the running host: the
unit exists on a gui host, ExecStart is the wrapped join, Install.WantedBy is
set so a wants link is actually made, Restart and RestartSec are pinned as a
pair, and headless and Darwin hosts get no unit. Eval failure is fatal rather
than being folded into a passing "the unit is absent" -- mari is the only
aarch64-darwin host and is evaluated from x86_64-linux, so it is the likeliest
of the six to break for reasons that have nothing to do with polkit, and the
gating cases would otherwise have read that breakage as correct. Same class as
f242ab9. Comparisons are exact rather than globbed, since `*WAYLAND_DISPLAY*`
also matches the negated spelling that inverts the gate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
